newsitem.title: USA: Clinton honors departing Defense Secretary Perry.
newsitem.headline: Clinton honors departing Defense Secretary Perry.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday awarded departing Defence Secretary William Perry the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honour, praising him for candor, clarity and integrity.

Clinton bestowed the star-shaped, blue-ribboned medal on Perry in an elaborate ceremony at Fort Myer in suburban Arlington, Virginia, with a musical salute and an honour guard representing the military's four services.
Perry, 69, told Clinton last year that he planned to leave government service after the grueling schedule he has kept as defence secretary for the past three years.
Clinton was lavish in his praise of Perry, a former Stanford University mathematics professor who took on the job of running the government's largest department in January, 1994.

"He set aside his love of mathematics and engineering to serve in demanding levels of government where the clarity and precision of his training and insight and ability were highly valued and sorly needed," Clinton said. "He did so with remarkable distinction, accomplishment and integrity."

"(Former President) Teddy Roosevelt said that those of us in positions of authority should speak softly and carry a big stick," Clinton said. "Bill Perry spoke softly and carried the biggest stick in the world with great care and to great effect."
Accepting the medal, Perry offered a strong defence of an activist U.S. role in the world, evoking Robert Frost's poem "The road not taken."
"This century has taught us that the road of isolation and apathy leads to instability and war," Perry said. "President Clinton chose the road of engagement and action."
Clinton has nominated William Cohen, a former U.S. Senator from Maine, to replace Perry. If confirmed by the Senate, as expected, Cohen would be the only Republican in the Cabinet.
Perry has said that he plans to return to California, where he expects to spend the next year writing a book on defence issues.
